standards.name: Systems Biology Ontology (SBO)
standards.abstract: An ontology (controlled, relational vocabularies) for systems biology and computational modeling. It defines vocabularies for reaction participant roles, quantitative parameters, classifications of mathematical expressions (rate laws), modeling frameworks, and branches describing entity and interaction types. Terms are provided as OWL/OBO files and browsable via the EBI Ontology Lookup Service.

classification.rationale: SBO is an ontology with many structured terms and classes; representing key classes/fields as a metadata table best captures the information-dense content for reuse and annotation.

systems_biology_representation.name: systems biology representation
systems_biology_representation.descr: Representation of an entity used in a systems biology knowledge reconstruction, such as a model, pathway, network.
systems_biology_representation.evidence: Representation of an entity used in a systems biology knowledge reconstruction, such as a model, pathway, network.

rate_law.descr: mathematical description that relates quantities of reactants to the reaction velocity.

quantitative_parameter.name: quantitative systems description parameter
quantitative_parameter.descr: A numerical value that defines certain characteristics of systems or system functions. It may be part of a calculation, but its value is not determined by the form of the equation itself, and may be arbitrarily assigned.

mass_action_rate_law.name: mass action rate law
mass_action_rate_law.descr: The Law of Mass Action... states that the speed of a chemical reaction is proportional to the quantity of the reacting substances. More formally, the change of a product quantity is proportional to the product of reactant activities. ... In the case of a well-stirred aqueous medium, the activities are equal to the concentrations.
mass_action_rate_law.evidence: The Law of Mass Action, first expressed by Waage and Guldberg in 1864 (Waage, P.; Guldberg, C. M. Forhandlinger: Videnskabs-Selskabet i Christiana 1864, 35) states that the speed of a chemical reaction is proportional to the quantity of the reacting substances. More formally, the change of a product quantity is proportional to the product of reactant activities. In the case of a reaction occurring in a gas phase, the activities are equal to the partial pressures. In the case of a well-stirred aqueous medium, the activities are equal to the concentrations. In the case of discrete kinetic description, the quantity are expressed in number of molecules and the relevant volume are implicitely embedded in the kinetic constant.

reactant.name: reactant
reactant.descr: Substance consumed by a chemical reaction. Reactants react with each other to form the products of a chemical reaction. In a chemical equation the Reactants are the elements or compounds on the left hand side of the reaction equation. A reactant can be consumed and produced by the same reaction, its global quantity remaining unchanged.
reactant.evidence: Substance consumed by a chemical reaction. Reactants react with each other to form the products of a chemical reaction. In a chemical equation the Reactants are the elements or compounds on the left hand side of the reaction equation. A reactant can be consumed and produced by the same reaction, its global quantity remaining unchanged.

product.name: product
product.descr: Substance that is produced in a reaction. In a chemical equation the Products are the elements or compounds on the right hand side of the reaction equation. A product can be produced and consumed by the same reaction, its global quantity remaining unchanged.

access_and_browsing.name: access / browsing
access_and_browsing.descr: SBO terms can be browsed through the Ontology Lookup Service (OLS) webpage and accessed via the OLS API.
access_and_browsing.evidence: SBO terms can be browsed through the Ontology Lookup Service (OLS) webpage https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/sbo .  Follow the documentation at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/docs/api to use API to access OLS web services for SBO.

license_and_project.name: license / project status
license_and_project.descr: SBO is an Open Biomedical Ontologies (OBO) candidate ontology, free for use, and a project of the BioModels.net effort developed through community collaboration.
license_and_project.evidence: SBO is an Open Biomedical Ontologies (OBO) candidate ontology, and is free for use. SBO is a project of the BioModels.net effort and is developed through community collaboration.

standards.notes: Extracted fields are representative examples and top-level classes/branches from the SBO README and OWL export. The SBO distribution contains many more specific terms (OWL/obo files) which are accessible via the provided OLS link or the repository.
